title: Record a resource baseline
goal: Capture a dated baseline before diagnosing a performance problem.
challenge: Create a guest-local baseline recording CPU count, load, available memory and filesystem space/inodes. Explain at least two limits of a single snapshot; do not claim a fault solely from an idle or busy value.

steps.explanation: Create a unique private guest workspace. Retain its printed path; repeat starts a new workspace, never overwrites old evidence. Stop if creation/change-directory fails.
steps.expected: A new /home/learner/capacity-baseline.XXXXXX directory. All files below are guest-local.

steps.explanation: Record time, available CPUs and load averages.
steps.expected: Values describe this virtual guest; load is not CPU percentage.

steps.explanation: Compare memory availability, usable KiB and inodes.
steps.expected: Available memory is different from free memory; byte and inode capacity are separate.

steps.explanation: Take three bounded samples. The first is normally an average since boot; later rows describe intervals.
steps.expected: The command returns after about two seconds; quiet or varying samples are valid.

steps.command: { date -Is; nproc; uptime; free -m; df -Pk .; df -Pi .; } > baseline.txt; cat baseline.txt
steps.explanation: Save and inspect a small timestamped snapshot.
steps.expected: A guest-local baseline, not historical monitoring or proof of a bottleneck.

hints: Start with units: CPUs, percentages, MiB, KiB and inode counts are different.
Use the available column in free, and do not equate load with percent CPU.
Record the sampling interval and guest context before proposing a cause.
review: I retained a timestamped baseline with units.
I distinguished a snapshot from a trend and named virtualization limits.
coverage: Partial 200.1 baseline resource observations; no network or full bottleneck diagnosis. Completion records self-review, not verified guest assessment; there is no score.
